programme.title: Sortilegio
programme.desc: Alejandro returns home after a terrible accident to discover that he is married to Maria Jose, a poor, innocent girl who was deceived by Alejandro's brother Bruno. Bruno used Alejandro's name to marry Maria Jose, soon after he sent to kill his brother in hopes that Maria Jose would inherit Alejandro's fortune. But when Maria Jose arrives at the mansion she realizes that Bruno lied to her and used her. She is also scared when Alejandro is found alive and returns home. Doctors tell Alejandro that he suffers from memory loss but he is convinced he never met Maria Jose before and goes in search of the truth, but during this time and Maria Jose actually fall in love, while Bruno and Maura (Alejandro's ex-girlfriend) plot to break them up. Meanwhile, the brothers' mother Victoria has fallen in love with Fernando--Alejandro's best friend, so closer to his age than hers.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: Franco finds out Mia isn't with Carlo and Roberta. Paola begs for Diego's forgiveness, which he gives, but refuses to take her back. Mia and Gastón go out on a date. Roberta ruins Simon's date by saying she's pregnant and underage.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: Nico breaks up with Karen. Gastón tells Mia he wants to speak to her dad. Teo receives a gift. Simon plans to get Roberta back for flattening his tires. programme.desc: León gives Diego a brand new car; Roberta crashes it. Gastón confronts Mia about her lingering feelings for Miguel. The Lodge figures out Miguel took Teo place; the later kidnap and torture Teo. Miguel and Mia kiss. Nico is told by Karen's father that the band is no longer welcome at his club. Giovanni, Diego, and Tomás put Madariaga's picture on an online dating site.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: Nico is upset about Karen's father, Jacobo's, decision about the band. Gastón orders Mia to call her father so they can talk. Teo is tied up by the Lodge and tortured. Diego finds out it was Roberta who crashed his car. Viviana misleads Franco to get Mia in trouble. The other band members try to convince Diego to come back to the band; without him they can't perform at the club. José's tutor comes to take her out but also to tell her to get close to Gastón. Gastón follows Mia and sees the band.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: The band finds out Gastón saw them perform; Miguel blames Mia, the others agree. Giovanni tries to rescue Teo but they are both caught and tortured. Nico tells his mother that he is in love with Lupita, not Karen. It's revealed that Pilar is in the Lodge. Viviana threatens Mia that she will tell Franco; later writes a fake fan letter even after Miguel asked her not to. Nico's mom tells Lupita to break up with Nico if she loves him.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: Giovanni climbs through the vents, onto the roof, then falls where he is later found by Tomás and Lupita. Gastón rebuffs Mia. Roberta disrespectfully embarrasses Alma in front of Carlo and the others; however she is mistaken. Madariaga and the other boys help save Teo.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: Gandia and Mendiola want to act like the Lodge doesn't exist. Miguel tries to draw the Lodge out. Franco tells Mia that Valeria will move in. Giovanni reflects on the good and bad. José makes a deal with Gastón so she can see Teo; she tells his father she's his girlfriend; she reveals her true feelings.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: José kisses Teo after revealing her feelings; though he's unconscious. programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.sub-title: Lovett or Leave It (These Gays, They’re Trying to Investigate Me!)
programme.desc: The Trump White House threatens Democrats who would dare to investigate the administration. Jensen Huang throws in the towel at Nvidia, and yes, his towel is made of leather too. And then Gianmarco Soresi, X Mayo, and drag king Murray Hill join to talk comedy and censorship, working at the TSA when MJ died, and drag culture before it became pop culture. Plus the Rant Wheel has us reeling over conservative outrage at Dave Chappell, Love Is Blind’s blindspots, Enes Kanter’s pathetic WNBA stunt, and certain wardrobe red flags.

programme.title: Pod Save America
programme.desc: Elon Musk tries to walk back his support of Republicans, saying that he’s “not MAGA,” that it was “foolish” to spend so much money on GOP candidates, and that Gina Hinojosa actually seems like a pretty good governor. Jon and Tommy react to Elon and other tech tycoons embracing woke 3.0, Trump’s chummy three-way meeting in China with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, his commitment to protect America’s “geniuses” amid allegations that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy, and his advice to Americans worried about major tech outages to “relax.” Then they discuss Hakeem Jeffries locking up the nomination for Speaker of the House, the latest on Chris Van Hollen’s challenge to Chuck Schumer, and Republicans — including Trump — beginning to turn on JD Vance.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (Trump’s Photo-Op, Xi and Putin’s Power Play)
programme.desc: President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin held an unprecedented trilateral meeting in China today. Joining guest host Todd Zwillich to break down what came out of the talks—and whether the meeting produced anything more than a photo-op—is Lingling Wei, chief China correspondent for The Wall Street Journal.

programme.title: Runaway Country with Alex Wagner
programme.sub-title: Runaway Country with Alex Wagner (Jensen’s Honeypot Becomes Trump’s Jackpot)
programme.desc: Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy is bad enough…but what turned out to be a honeypot for the former Nvidia CEO has been a jackpot for the Trump White House—particularly for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Alex is joined by CNN’s Chief Domestic Correspondent Phil Mattingly to unpack Lutnick’s shady AI chip policy, whether he’s lining his family’s pockets with overseas data centers, and what Trump has gained from letting Nvidia run wild. Then, she puts it all into context with Congressman Jim Himes—the incoming chair of the House Committee on Intelligence and a member of the House Financial Services Committee—to understand what this grift means for American national security, and what Democrats can do about it.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (Is SCOTUS Shifting After The Midterms?)
programme.desc: It’s been two weeks since the Democrats swept the midterms, and the Supreme Court has upheld a legal defeat for President Trump over his anti-DEI agenda. On today’s show, Jane talks with Kate Shaw, co-host of Strict Scrutiny, about whether this signals a changing tide or is just a blip.

programme.desc: What can 100+ farms teach us about big bucks? To answer it, Jake is joined by Jack Huston with Midwest Deer Surveys, who has flown hundreds of properties with thermal drones and seen exactly where deer are - and more importantly, where they aren’t. From density rings and social stress to bedding, pressure, and why “thicker” farms consistently produce, this episode challenges a lot of conventional thinking. We also get into how doe harvest impacts herds over time, what role genetics actually play, and why many hunters don’t struggle killing deer.

programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with author of The Loves Of Theodore Roosevelt and CEO of the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, Ed O'Keefe. Joined by Randall Williams, Phil Taylor, and Corinne Schneider. Topics discussed: The ladies in Teddy's life; being a sickly child and powering through pain; hunting to study; a tremendous taxidermy collection; a family that founded so many museums; sisters as advisors and confidants; a life-altering Valentine's Day tragedy; when a thick manuscript in your front jacket pocket stops a bullet and saves your life; being the first president to embrace women's suffrage and the right to own property; one of the most beloved in American history; and more.
